reads: every tools/*.mjs, comment-blanked, against the two shapes the brief published as greps. The shape is not the exposure: an adopter still matches its own shape, so this gate subtracts an adopter BY NAME.

write.enumeratedWith: the brief §1 grep: a root from `import.meta.url`, filtered by `writeFileSync` or `appendFileSync`
write.adoptedMeans: the tool calls writeRoot or writeRootOrDie where the write happens
write.pendingMeans: the tool matches the shape and owes one reading in its own header (brief §3). A name leaves this list only by adopting, or with the file.
write.exemptMeans: the regexes read the tool’s own test data. Each row carries the sentence that says why, and a mute row reds.

tools/absence-ledger.mjs.reading: `--write` writes a tracked work-unit artifact, `audits/ABSENCE-SURVEY-2026-09-22-STATE.json`, which a wrong checkout loses; every read keeps its own reach, so another checkout may still import `LEDGER`

tools/ecg-physionet-differential.mjs.reading: `--pin` writes a tracked work-unit artifact, `tools/physionet-mitdb-manifest.json`; the selftest corpus stays in `mkdtempSync(tmpdir())`, outside every checkout

tools/new-changeset.mjs.reading: it writes a tracked work-unit artifact, `changes/<slug>.md`, which a wrong checkout loses (row 2026-11-02-a-tool-run-by-absolute-path-writes-into-its-own-checkout)

tools/release.mjs.reading: it stamps five tracked files — `suite.manifest.json`, `CITATION.cff`, `RELEASE-MANIFEST.json`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `README.md` — and unlinks every consumed changeset, so a cross-checkout run cuts a release in a tree nobody named; `release-land.mjs` runs the stamp as a relative path under the worktree’s own cwd, so both call sites already agree; a `--status` report reads a state file and writes no tracked artifact, so the guard sits on the stamp and `--full` branches only

tools/repo-map.mjs.reading: `--write` puts the shared repo map in the git common dir of ONE checkout and `doc-search` never rebuilds it, so a run by absolute path from another checkout left the caller’s own tree answering from a stale map at exit 0; the guard sits on the `--write` branch alone, and `writeMap` keeps its injected `root` so the selftest still writes under `mkdtemp`

tools/sync-docs-index.mjs.reading: it rewrites the tracked `DOCS-INDEX.md` that `docs-ledger` check3b judges, so a wrong checkout both loses the fix and reds a tree nobody is editing; `--check` writes nothing

tools/tools-index.mjs.reading: it generates `docs/TOOLS-INDEX.md`, which `npm run verify:tools-index` re-checks in CI, so a write into the wrong checkout reds a job the causing worktree cannot explain

tools/verdict-adoption.mjs.reading: `--format` rewrites the tracked `tools/verdict-adoption.json` it resolves from its own root, so a cross-checkout run rewrites the shared root’s manifest and leaves the worktree unchanged; every selftest read keeps its own reach

exempt.tools/consensus-polarity-wiring.mjs: both writes sit in its selftest, which makes one `mkdtempSync(tmpdir())` sandbox, plants a file and a broken symlink inside it and removes it; the tool writes no tracked artifact, writes nothing under any checkout, and calls no write wrapper
exempt.tools/nsrr-effort-typing.mjs: its one write plants four filename fixtures in a selftest `mkdtempSync(tmpdir())` directory, so the write regex reads its own test data; it writes no tracked artifact and calls no write wrapper
exempt.tools/pr-compliance.mjs: both writes build a two-changeset fixture repo inside a selftest `mkdtempSync(tmpdir())` directory, so the write regex reads its own test data; the gate writes no tracked artifact and calls no write wrapper
exempt.tools/read-ref-drift.mjs: both write calls sit in its selftest, which builds a two-clone git fixture under mkdtemp and removes it; the tool writes no tracked artifact, writes nothing under any checkout, and calls no write wrapper
exempt.tools/ste-lint.mjs: its one write builds a `docs/GLOSSARY.md` fixture inside a selftest `mkdtempSync(tmpdir())` directory, so the write regex reads its own test data; it writes no tracked artifact and calls no write wrapper
exempt.tools/write-root-adoption.mjs: its selftests plant both shapes as fixture strings, so the write regexes read its own test data; it writes no tracked artifact and calls no write wrapper
exempt.tools/write-targets.mjs: every write call and every wrapper name in it is a fixture string in `PLANT` or a detection regex, so both shapes read the tool’s own test data; the census prints to stdout, writes no tracked artifact, and calls no write wrapper

judge.enumeratedWith: the brief §6.2 grep: a verdict, `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`, and that root as a child `cwd`
judge.adoptedMeans: the tool calls judgeRoot or judgeRootOrDie where the judge happens
judge.pendingMeans: the tool matches the shape and owes one reading in its own header (brief §6.4). A name leaves this list only by adopting, or with the file.
judge.exemptMeans: the tool spawns no child that judges a tree. Its only child asks `git rev-parse` for a commit stamp, which names the code that produced the verdict and is right in the checkout of the tool itself. Each row carries the sentence that says why, and a mute row reds.

tools/astgrep-gate.mjs.reading: it scans the tracked source of the tree it resolves, under that tree's own rules and allow-list, so a cross-checkout run would scan another work-unit's source and call the answer this branch's

tools/bus-conf-provenance.mjs.reading: it censuses the *-dsp.js files of the tree it resolves and reads that tree’s base ref, so a cross-checkout run would judge another work-unit’s DSP sources and call the answer this branch’s

tools/detector-change-advisory.mjs.reading: it reconciles the declared detector sets against the root `*.js` and `capture-host/` files of the tree it resolves, and censuses that tree's diff against a base ref, so a cross-checkout run would reconcile another work-unit's files and call the answer this branch's

tools/flag-exit-drive.mjs.reading: it reads each recipe's source in the tree it resolves and spawns that copy as a child, so a cross-checkout run would drive another work-unit's tools and call the answer this branch's

tools/hook-contract.mjs.reading: it judges `.claude/hooks` and `package.json` of the tree it resolves, so a cross-checkout run would judge another work-unit's hooks and call the answer this branch's

tools/integrator-surface-gate.mjs.reading: it reads integrator-dsp.js, every declared reader realm and the surface declaration of the tree it resolves, and it stamps producedBy.commit from a git call in that tree, so a cross-checkout run judged another work-unit's 148 keys and printed PASS at exit 0

tools/judge-targets.mjs.reading: it reads the manifest of the judge arm and the tracked source of every tool the arm names, so a cross-checkout run would census the tools of another work-unit and attribute the answer to this branch

tools/killcheck.mjs.reading: it hard-links the tree it resolves into each worker and runs that copy's suite against recorded mutants, so a cross-checkout run would score another work-unit's source and call the kill rate this branch's

tools/residue-path-leads.mjs.reading: it reads a ref and a git log with `cwd: REPO`, so a cross-checkout run would report another checkout's ledger as this one's

tools/run-check.mjs.reading: it runs the whole local gate in the tree it resolves, so a cross-checkout run would judge another work-unit

tools/secret-scan.mjs.reading: it judges the commits the RUN’s branch adds (#4384, row 2026-11-04-a-verdict-gate-judges-the-checkout-it-lives-in-not-the-one-it-ran-from)

tools/workflow-timeout-guard.mjs.reading: it judges `.github/workflows` of the tree it resolves, so a cross-checkout run would judge another work-unit's workflow caps and call the answer this branch's

tools/write-root-adoption.mjs.reading: it censuses the tool tree of the RUN’s work-unit and publishes a verdict about it
